title: How does coax enforce its own policy on the agent's tool calls?
body:
Today a Claude profile's `settings.json` runs `hooks/git-guard.py` as a PreToolUse command hook on Bash. The script blocks `git push` and `gh pr merge`. It also checks commit messages and `gh` bodies for the credit line. When it blocks a call, Jack has no way to let that one call through. He has to edit the rule or run the command himself.

coax answers each `session/request_permission` in `Link` (`src/acp.rs`). It shows the request as a permission box, and the person's choice goes back as `RequestPermissionOutcome`. coax advertises `fs` read and write and `terminal(false)`. In `auto` mode, Claude Code sends no request for a call it judges safe (coax-419109), so coax sees only some calls.

The goal is to move tool-call policy into coax. A blocked command should become a box Jack can answer "allow once". Hooks should also stop depending on a shell command plus whatever Claude Code does with its answer.

## What the Claude adapter v0.101.0 allows

These come from reading the adapter's bundle and the bundled `claude` binary. Nothing here has been tested live.

- The adapter's `canUseTool` sends `session/request_permission` whenever Claude Code's permission check ends in ask. That covers every tool kind, MCP tools included. `AskUserQuestion` goes through elicitation instead.
- `toolCall.rawInput` is the model's input unchanged. It holds the whole Bash `command`, an edit's `file_path`, `old_string` and `new_string`, a write's `content`, and MCP arguments.
- `_meta.claudeCode.options.settings` on `session/new` becomes Claude Code's `--settings`. Inline `permissions.ask`, `deny` and `allow` rules apply to that session. `disallowedTools` entries act as deny rules. `settings.hooks` accepts command hooks. SDK `options.hooks` take JS callbacks only, so a client cannot send them.
- The user's own settings, their hooks included, still load. `settingSources` in the same options can narrow that.
- Claude Code splits a compound Bash command and checks each part. A deny on any part denies the whole command, and an ask on any part asks. So `cd x && git push` matches `Bash(git push:*)`.
- A `cd` followed by a git command raises its own ask.
- The answer to a request carries only an option id, or `cancelled`. It has no reason field and no rewritten input. A refusal reaches the model as the fixed text "User refused permission to run tool".
- When an ask rule matched, the adapter offers only `allow-once` and `reject`. It offers no "always" option.
- Claude Code runs Bash and the file tools inside its own process. The adapter never calls `terminal/create`, and nothing calls its `fs` forwarding methods. So a client cannot gate execution through those capabilities.
- The adapter has no other way for a client to veto or rewrite a call before it runs. ACP has none either, stable or draft. The v2 permission-requests RFD in Preview adds a `command` subject with `cwd`, but no reason and no rewrite.

The permission order in Claude Code's core check, as read from minified code:

```text
1. tool-level deny            -> deny
2. deny rule                  -> deny (coax never hears of it)
3. tool-wide ask rule         -> ask
4. the tool's own check       -> deny if it denies
5. content ask rule           -> ask, with matchedAskRule
6. requiresUserInteraction    -> ask
7. permission mode            -> bypassPermissions allows here
8. allow rules                -> allow
9. anything left              -> ask
```

So an ask rule should reach coax in `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan` and `auto`. In `auto`, Claude Code logs `tengu_auto_mode_fallback_to_ask` and skips its classifier. In `bypassPermissions` it should still ask, but an SDK warning string says the opposite. `dontAsk` turns every ask into a deny without asking. A headless session that sets `shouldAvoidPermissionPrompts` does the same.

## Options

| Option | What coax gets | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Ask rules and a coax policy | Sees every call a rule routes to it, and allows, refuses or asks | The model cannot learn why a call was refused |
| A hook command that coax owns | A reason the model sees, and a rewritten input | Still a shell command under Claude Code's hook protocol |
| coax runs the tools itself | Full control of every call | Rebuilding Bash, Edit and the rest as MCP tools |

### Ask rules and a coax policy

coax passes ask rules on `session/new`. A broad rule such as `Bash` sends coax every shell command, and a narrow one such as `Bash(git push:*)` sends only those. A policy in `config.toml` matches on `rawInput` and returns one of three outcomes. It can allow, refuse, or show the box with the policy's reason in it. `git-guard.py` comes out of the profile.

A broad `Bash` rule takes Claude Code's `auto` classifier out of the loop for Bash. Any command the policy does not match would then need the person, or a default.

The adapter queues a prompt sent during a turn and gives it to the model with the next tool result (`claude-adapter-queues-prompts`). On a refusal, coax could send a short prompt that says why. The model would see it as a message from the person, and no one has tried it.

### A hook command that coax owns

coax passes `settings.hooks` with a PreToolUse hook such as `coax hook`, which asks the running coax over a socket. Claude Code's hook answer can deny with a reason the model sees, or allow with an updated input. Jack wants to move away from exactly this shape. In return it closes both gaps that permission requests leave.

### coax runs the tools itself

`_meta.disableBuiltInTools` empties the tool list, and coax supplies its own tools over MCP. It gives full control, and it loses Claude Code's Bash handling, sandboxing and edit previews. This option is rejected unless the other two fail.

The lean is the first option, since it needs no hook at all. The coax-owned hook would come later, only if the model needs to know why a call was refused.

## Open

- Does an ask rule reach coax in `auto` and in `bypassPermissions`? A trial run with a real `session/new` settles it.
- How do `git -C dir push`, `VAR=x git push` and `xargs git push` match an ask rule?
- Where do PreToolUse hooks run in the order above?
- What does the model see after a refusal, and does a queued prompt reach it in time?
- What form does the policy take in `config.toml`: patterns over `rawInput`, a command coax runs, or both?
